label: Liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma)

approval.note: Draft checklist from the NCG GI guideline on hepatocellular carcinoma: needs a clinician's check

site_note: V2 item 5.3 (two primaries): only on a Case File linked to the same patient's other Case File, and only for histopathology, cytology, IHC and molecular records: among several candidates for one record, or several documents carrying a required value, one that names another protocol's site and not this one steps aside and is named on the row for review; a document naming no site never does, and when every candidate names another site every candidate stays. Organ words only. A preference, never a filter; a patient with one cancer is checked as before.
note: Draft checklist from the NCG GI guideline on hepatocellular carcinoma (a Word file with no page numbers: each source names its section): needs a clinician's check. The file's key reads 'Normal font- Essential, Underlined -desirable, italics- optional'; the tier of each work-up item was read from that formatting (normal font Essential, underlined Optimal, italics Optional). Tiers marked proposed are proposals, to be confirmed by the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). PET: the NOTES say 'FDG PET CT has no role in routine evaluation or follow up of HCC', so no PET record is listed. Child class, HKLC, BCLC and LI-RADS are recorded as the report states them and never computed; poor liver function (Child C) is a recorded fact, not a setting. No treatment advice. India first: the National Cancer Grid guideline is the only source (hepatitis B and C also need evaluation, and cost in India is noted in the NOTES).
settings_note: The setting of the Case File, chosen by the clinician from what the signed reports record (the system never computes a stage and never decides the setting). Each record carries its tier per setting; until a setting is recorded the strictest tier applies. Draft checklist: needs a clinician's check.

post_board.record_fields_source: EUSOMA 2020 (names of all participants, evidence on decisions); Victorian Cancer MDM quality framework 2018 (report errors/changes raised, divergent recommendations and dissenting clinicians); PM-JAY HBP 2.2 s.3.9 (tumour board decision and treatment plan)

policy_basis: PM-JAY Health Benefit Package 2.2 user guidelines (NHA, 2021), section 3.9: pre-authorization is mandatory at each step of cancer care and the decision on appropriate care is to be taken by a multidisciplinary tumour board; NHS England MDT streamlining guidance (2020) pre-listing conditions. The NCG book itself asks for the board: "The decision should be taken by a multidisciplinary team." (NCG GI: Hepatocellular carcinoma, NOTES, ablation paragraph); the Tumour Board Case File is that discussion, so no separate record is required for it (orchestrator, night-v3 Phase 2).
